interpretive.purpose: A repository containing various .NET projects demonstrating configuration management, dependency injection, exception handling, and API development.
consumers: Developers looking to understand configuration patterns in .NET
Teams implementing dependency injection for better code maintainability
Users interested in exception handling best practices
API developers needing a simple API setup

components.name: Configuration.cs
components.responsibility: Contains basic class definitions without specific responsibilities.

components.name: AppSettings.cs
components.responsibility: Defines configuration settings for the application, including nested settings.

components.name: GenericClassOptions.cs
components.responsibility: Provides a template for options classes used in dependency injection.

components.name: Program.cs (Configurations)
components.responsibility: Sets up and binds configuration sources, demonstrating various configuration methods.

components.name: Program.cs (ConsoleUI)
components.responsibility: Demonstrates global exception handling with a console application.

components.name: Program.cs (DependencyInjection)
components.responsibility: Illustrates different types of dependency injection: constructor, setter, and interface injection.

components.name: IMessageWriter.cs
components.responsibility: Defines an interface for writing messages.

components.name: MessageWriter.cs
components.responsibility: Implements the IMessageWriter interface to write messages to the console.

components.name: Program.cs (DependencyInjection.Example1)
components.responsibility: Sets up a hosted service with dependency injection using an interface.

components.name: Worker.cs
components.responsibility: A background service that writes messages at regular intervals.

components.name: Program.cs (DependencyInjection1)
components.responsibility: Initializes a ServiceCollection for dependency injection setup.

components.name: DemoCode.cs
components.responsibility: Demonstrates exception handling with nested try-catch blocks and rethrowing exceptions.

components.name: GlobalUsings.cs (SampleApi)
components.responsibility: Contains global using directives for the SampleApi project.

components.name: Program.cs (SampleApi)
components.responsibility: Sets up a web application with OpenAPI support and HTTPS redirection.

components.name: Program.cs (TesteUI)
components.responsibility: Configures a Blazor WebAssembly host for client-side UI development.

interpretive.data_flow_summary: This is a grab-bag of independent, mostly-unrelated .NET learning samples in one solution, not a single application, so there is no data flow spanning the whole repo. Within SampleApi specifically: minimal-API endpoints (SampleApi/Endpoints) call DataAccess, which uses Dapper + Microsoft.Data.SqlClient to invoke stored procedures against the UserDB SQL Server database project. The other folders (Configurations, ConsoleUI, DependencyInjection*, ExceptionsLibrary, TestUI/TesteUI) are standalone demos with no cross-project calls.

integration_points.name: SQL Server (UserDB)
integration_points.description: SampleApi's /users endpoints read/write via DataAccess's Dapper + Microsoft.Data.SqlClient wrapper, calling stored procedures (dbo.spUser_*) defined in the UserDB SQL Server database project.

operational_notes: Ensure that user secrets are not checked into version control.
Configuration files should be named correctly to match the environment (e.g., appsettings.Development.json).
Dependency injection setup requires careful management of service lifetimes and scopes.

ExceptionsLibrary/DemoCode.cs has a stray extra closing brace after the class and fails to compile (verified via `dotnet build`) as of the distilled commit; ConsoleUI, which references ExceptionsLibrary, will not build until that is fixed.
